home.discoverBuildingBlocks: Discover the Building Blocks of the Universe
home.exploreDescription: Explore all 118 chemical elements through interactive 3D atomic structures, real-world applications, chemical reactions, and discovery histories.
home.searchPlaceholder: Search any element by Name (Gold), Symbol (Au), or Number (79)...
home.goldDesc: A dense, soft, malleable, and highly ductile metal with a bright yellow metallic luster. Extremely resistant to corrosion and chemical oxidation.
home.timelineDesc: Trace the human journey of isolating chemical elements, from antiquity's metals to modern synthetic superheavy elements.

timeline.antiquityDesc: Known since prehistoric times by ancient civilizations.
timeline.t1669Desc: First element scientifically isolated by Hennig Brand.
timeline.t1774Desc: Isolated by Joseph Priestley and Carl Wilhelm Scheele.
timeline.t1869Desc: Dmitri Mendeleev arranged 63 known elements into the first periodic table.
timeline.t2016Desc: Period 7 completed with official recognition of superheavy element 118.

footer.description: Making Chemistry Simple, Interactive & Accessible. Exploring the 118 chemical elements through 3D visualizations, periodic trends, and scientific accuracy.

contact.title: Contact FRZI Labs
contact.desc: Have questions, scientific corrections, suggestions, or collaboration proposals? We would love to hear from you.
contact.emailDesc: Click the button below to send an email directly to our development and support team via your default mail client.
contact.reportDesc: If you spot any numerical inaccuracies in atomic mass, density, oxidation states, or electron configuration, please report them so we can update the dataset immediately.
contact.suggestDesc: Have an idea for a new 3D visualization, interactive periodic trend tool, or quiz feature? Send us your suggestions to help improve chemistry learning.
contact.collabDesc: We welcome partnerships with chemistry educators, academic institutions, science communicators, and open-source science initiatives.
contact.eduDesc: Interested in using FRZI Labs interactive 3D Periodic Table in your school or university curriculum? Feel free to contact us for guidance.
